topic_title: Top 7 Best Dog Breeds That Get Along With Cats
intro: Living with a cat depends less on the breed label and more on chase instinct, energy and size. A calm dog that ignores a running cat is far easier than a bouncy one that treats every dash as a game. All seven breeds here are rated good with cats, but individual dogs vary, so ask breeders or rescues about each dog's history with cats. Plan the introduction over days or weeks, with separate spaces, scent swapping and a dog-free escape route such as a baby gate or tall cat tree.

picks.description: The Cavalier tops this list because its temperament is described as gentle, calm and affectionate, it is rated good with cats, kids and other dogs, and its barking is low, so it is unlikely to stress a nervous cat. At around 13 to 18 pounds it is close enough to cat size that play stays manageable, though some Cavaliers still flush birds and may follow a running cat until taught otherwise. Daily exercise of 30 to 45 minutes is plenty. The silky coat sheds moderately and needs brushing a few times a week. The main trade-offs are health and company: the breed is prone to heart disease, so choose a breeder who screens for it, and Cavaliers dislike long hours alone. Lifespan ranges from about 9 to 14 years.
picks.best_for: Cat owners who want a quiet, affectionate small dog at home
picks.quirky_fact: Cavaliers often settle near people rather than patrolling the house, which leaves cats plenty of undisturbed space.
picks.skip_if: You're away long hours or can't budget for potential heart care

picks.description: The Havanese is a small, sociable companion rated good with cats, kids and other dogs, with a temperament described as affectionate, playful and gentle. Its medium energy means 30 minutes or so of walks and indoor games covers most days, so it rarely has the pent-up energy that leads to chasing. Most Havanese weigh under 15 pounds, so even a lively one is unlikely to overpower a cat. It sheds little, but the long, silky coat tangles easily and needs brushing most days or a short trim every six to eight weeks. Barking is rated medium, so teach a quiet cue early. The Havanese is easy to train and can live 14 to 16 years, one of the longest spans on this list, but it bonds closely and copes poorly when left alone.
picks.best_for: Smaller homes wanting a low-shedding, cat-friendly, long-lived companion
picks.quirky_fact: The Havanese is the national dog of Cuba and was once a favorite of Cuban aristocracy.
picks.skip_if: You can't brush daily, pay for trims or keep someone home often

picks.description: The Bichon Frise is a cheerful small dog rated good with cats, kids and other dogs, with a temperament described as affectionate, playful and gentle. Its play style is bouncy rather than predatory, so with early guidance most Bichons learn to leave a cat alone or play gently. Daily exercise of 30 to 45 minutes, split between walks and indoor play, suits it well. The curly coat sheds little but grows constantly, so plan on brushing several times a week and professional grooming about every four to six weeks to prevent mats. Barking is rated medium, and Bichons can be slower to house-train than other easy-to-train breeds, so consistency helps. A lifespan of 12 to 15 years is typical.
picks.best_for: Cat households wanting a playful small dog that sheds little
picks.quirky_fact: Bichons were popular performers with traveling circuses and street entertainers in Europe because they learn tricks easily.
picks.skip_if: You don't want regular grooming bills or a dog that dislikes being alone

picks.description: The Great Dane is the surprise here: a giant breed whose temperament is described as gentle, calm and friendly, rated good with cats, kids and other dogs, and with low barking. Many Danes are content to lounge for much of the day once they have had 30 to 60 minutes of walking and play. The risk with a cat is size rather than aggression, since a playful swipe or a misplaced paw can hurt a small animal, so teach a reliable leave-it cue and give the cat high escape routes. Training is rated moderate, so start early, before the puppy outgrows you. The short coat needs only weekly brushing. Trade-offs include high food and vet costs, low heat tolerance and a short lifespan of about 7 to 10 years.
picks.best_for: Cat owners with space who want a calm, quiet big dog
picks.quirky_fact: Despite the name, the Great Dane was developed largely in Germany, where it is known as the Deutsche Dogge.
picks.skip_if: You have a small home, a hot climate or a tight budget

picks.description: The Golden Retriever is rated good with cats, kids and other dogs and has an affectionate, friendly temperament that usually adapts well to a cat once introduced carefully. It ranks mid-list because its energy is high: a young Golden's enthusiasm can overwhelm a cat, so expect a supervised adjustment period and keep the dog on a leash or behind a gate during early meetings. Plan on 60 to 90 minutes of exercise each day, which also helps keep it calm indoors. Goldens are easy to train, so a leave-it cue and settling on a mat come quickly. The double coat sheds heavily and needs brushing a few times a week. Lifespan is about 10 to 12 years, and hip and elbow screening is worth asking breeders about.
picks.best_for: Active families with a confident cat and time for daily exercise
picks.quirky_fact: Goldens were bred with a soft mouth for carrying game birds, so many gently carry toys around the house.
picks.skip_if: Your cat is timid or you can't manage heavy shedding and exercise

picks.description: The Standard Poodle is intelligent, easy to train and rated good with cats, kids and other dogs, and it sheds little, which helps in a home already dealing with cat hair. Its energy is high, and at 40 to 70 pounds it is a big, athletic dog, so the main challenge with a cat is its boisterousness rather than aggression. Steady training and 60 to 90 minutes of daily exercise plus mental games such as puzzle feeders keep it calm enough for a shared house. The curly coat needs brushing several times a week and professional grooming every four to six weeks. Barking is rated medium. Poodles are sensitive and people-focused, so they do best in homes with company for much of the day, and they often live 12 to 15 years.
picks.best_for: Owners wanting a trainable, low-shedding large dog in a cat home
picks.quirky_fact: The breed's name comes from the German 'Pudel', linked to splashing in water, reflecting its origins as a water retriever.
picks.skip_if: You can't commit to regular grooming and lots of daily exercise

picks.description: The English Springer Spaniel is friendly and easy to train and is rated good with cats, kids and other dogs, but it ranks last here because it is a high-energy bird dog bred to flush game. That instinct can make a fast-moving cat hard to ignore, especially for a young or under-exercised dog. With 60 to 90 minutes of daily exercise, early introductions and a strong leave-it cue, many Springers live peacefully with cats, and a confident cat that stands its ground usually helps. The medium, wavy coat sheds moderately and needs brushing a couple of times a week, with ear checks to prevent infections. Barking is rated medium, and Springers dislike long periods alone. Lifespan is typically 12 to 14 years.
picks.best_for: Active households with a confident cat and time for training
picks.quirky_fact: The name 'springer' refers to the breed's job of springing, or flushing, birds into the air for hunters.
picks.skip_if: Your cat is skittish or you can't give a long daily run

faqs.question: What dog breed is best for a home with cats?
faqs.answer: Calm, gentle breeds with low chase instinct suit cat homes best. On this list, the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel, Havanese and Bichon Frise lead because they are small, affectionate and rated good with cats. A dog's own history matters more than breed, so ask about past experience living with cats.

faqs.question: How do I introduce a dog to a cat?
faqs.answer: Keep them in separate rooms for the first days and swap bedding so each learns the other's scent. Then allow short, leashed meetings through a gate, rewarding the dog for calm behavior. Always give the cat high perches and a dog-free room, and increase time together gradually over several weeks.

faqs.question: Is a puppy or an adult dog better with cats?
faqs.answer: A puppy raised with a calm cat often learns to accept it, but puppies are boisterous and need close supervision. An adult dog with a known history of living peacefully with cats is the lower-risk choice, since you already know how it reacts. Rescues often cat-test dogs before adoption.

faqs.question: Which dog breeds are usually not good with cats?
faqs.answer: Breeds bred to chase or hunt small animals, such as many terriers and sighthounds, and some herding and guarding breeds are often rated not good with cats. In our data the German Shepherd and the Belgian herding breeds fall into that group. Individual dogs vary, but expect more training and management.

faqs.question: Can a large dog live safely with a cat?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the dog is calm and well trained. The Great Dane on this list is giant but rated gentle and good with cats. The risk with big dogs is accidental injury during play, so teach a solid leave-it cue and make sure the cat always has escape routes up high.
